title: Insurance and Pension Sector
desc: IRDAI, PMFBY, NPS, PFRDA and pension reforms

basic.q: What does IRDAI stand for?
o: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
Indian Reserve and Deposit Authority of India
Insurance Reserve and Depository Authority of India
Investment Regulatory and Development Authority of India
basic.e: IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India) is the statutory body that regulates and develops the insurance industry in India.

basic.q: Where is the headquarters of IRDAI located?
basic.e: IRDAI's head office is located in Hyderabad, Telangana.

basic.q: Under which Act was IRDAI constituted?
basic.e: IRDAI was established under the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999, which also opened the insurance sector to private and foreign players.

basic.q: In which year was the Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) of India established through nationalisation of life insurance business?
basic.e: Life insurance business in India was nationalised in 1956 with the formation of the Life Insurance Corporation (LIC).

basic.q: In which year was the general insurance business in India nationalised, leading to the formation of GIC?
basic.e: General insurance business was nationalised in 1972 through the General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act, forming the General Insurance Corporation (GIC).

basic.q: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) was launched in which year?
basic.e: PMFBY, the flagship crop insurance scheme, was launched in 2016, replacing earlier crop insurance schemes.

basic.q: Which schemes did the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) primarily replace?
o: National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS) and Modified NAIS
basic.e: PMFBY replaced the National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS) and the Modified NAIS (MNAIS) to provide a simplified, farmer-friendly crop insurance product.

basic.q: Under PMFBY, what is the uniform maximum premium payable by farmers for Kharif food and oilseed crops?
basic.e: Under PMFBY, farmers pay a uniform premium of 2% of the sum insured for Kharif food and oilseed crops.

basic.q: Under PMFBY, what is the uniform premium payable by farmers for Rabi food and oilseed crops?
basic.e: For Rabi food and oilseed crops under PMFBY, farmers pay a uniform premium of 1.5% of the sum insured.

basic.q: The National Pension System (NPS) was made mandatory for new recruits to central government service (except armed forces) joining on or after which date?
basic.e: NPS became mandatory for central government employees (excluding armed forces) who joined service on or after 1 January 2004.

basic.q: In which year was the National Pension System (NPS) opened voluntarily to all citizens of India, including private sector employees?
basic.e: NPS was extended on a voluntary basis to all Indian citizens, including private sector workers, from 2009.

basic.q: Which body regulates and promotes the National Pension System in India?
basic.e: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) regulates the National Pension System and pension funds in India.

basic.q: PFRDA was given statutory status under which Act?
basic.e: PFRDA, which functioned as an interim regulator from 2003, was granted statutory status under the PFRDA Act, 2013.

basic.q: In which year was the Atal Pension Yojana (APY) launched?
basic.e: Atal Pension Yojana was launched in 2015 to provide a guaranteed pension to workers in the unorganised sector.

basic.q: Under Atal Pension Yojana, subscribers can receive a guaranteed minimum monthly pension in which range, after age 60?
basic.e: APY guarantees a fixed monthly pension ranging from Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000, depending on the contribution and entry age.

basic.q: What is the eligible age band for joining the Atal Pension Yojana?
basic.e: Any Indian citizen aged between 18 and 40 years with a bank/post office account can join APY.

basic.q: Under the National Pension System, which account/tier is mandatory and has restrictions on withdrawal until retirement?
o: Both Tier I and Tier II equally
basic.e: Tier I is the mandatory, non-withdrawable pension account, while Tier II is a voluntary savings account with no withdrawal restrictions.

basic.q: Which public sector entity primarily undertakes reinsurance business in India as the national reinsurer?
basic.e: GIC Re (General Insurance Corporation of India) functions as India's national reinsurer, providing reinsurance support to insurance companies.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best distinguishes the Old Pension Scheme (OPS) from the National Pension System (NPS)?
o: OPS is a defined-contribution scheme while NPS is a defined-benefit scheme
OPS is a defined-benefit scheme funded entirely by the government while NPS is a defined-contribution scheme with employee and employer contributions
Both are defined-benefit schemes but differ only in retirement age
NPS guarantees a fixed pension amount while OPS does not
intermediate.e: Under OPS, the government paid a fixed pension (defined benefit) entirely from its own resources; under NPS, both employee and employer contribute to a pension corpus invested in market-linked instruments (defined contribution).

intermediate.q: Which institution administers the Atal Pension Yojana on the ground through banks and post offices, while PFRDA acts as the regulator?
intermediate.e: The NPS Trust, under PFRDA's oversight, administers APY, with participating banks and post offices acting as points of presence for subscriber enrolment.

intermediate.q: What is the primary purpose of the Insurance Ombudsman mechanism in India?
o: To set premium rates for all insurers
To provide an inexpensive and speedy forum for resolving policyholder grievances against insurers
intermediate.e: The Insurance Ombudsman scheme offers policyholders a low-cost, quick grievance redressal mechanism against insurers, without needing to go to court.

intermediate.q: 'Bancassurance' refers to which of the following arrangements?
o: Banks providing insurance directly as an in-house department without any tie-up
Banks acting as corporate agents to distribute insurance products of insurance companies
Insurance companies taking over commercial banks
A government scheme guaranteeing bank deposits
intermediate.e: Bancassurance is an arrangement where banks, using their branch network, sell insurance products of insurers as corporate agents in return for a fee/commission.

intermediate.q: Under PMFBY, how is the premium subsidy (the difference between actuarial premium and the farmer's share) typically shared between the Centre and States?
o: Borne entirely by the Central Government
Equally shared between Centre and State Governments, with a higher Central share for North-Eastern States
Shared between insurance companies and farmers only
intermediate.e: The premium subsidy under PMFBY is generally shared equally between the Centre and State Governments, with the Centre bearing a higher share for North-Eastern states to encourage participation.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about General Insurance in India is correct?
o: General insurance covers only life-related risks
General insurance includes health, motor, fire and marine insurance, among others
General insurance policies are always for a lifetime term
General insurance is regulated by PFRDA
intermediate.e: General insurance covers non-life risks such as health, motor, fire, marine and other property/liability risks, and is regulated by IRDAI, not PFRDA.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. IRDAI is a statutory body established by an Act of Parliament. 2. IRDAI licenses both life and general insurance companies operating in India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: IRDAI was set up under the IRDA Act, 1999 (a statutory body), and it is responsible for licensing and regulating both life and general insurers in India.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Under NPS, the government makes an unconditional guarantee of a minimum fixed return to subscribers. 2. NPS returns are market-linked and depend on the performance of underlying pension fund investments. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — NPS, being a defined-contribution scheme, does not guarantee a fixed return; returns depend on market performance of the chosen investment mix, making statement 2 correct.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Atal Pension Yojana provides a guaranteed pension regardless of market returns. 2. The government does not contribute anything to any subscriber's APY account. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct — APY guarantees a fixed pension. Statement 2 is incorrect — the government had earlier provided a co-contribution for eligible subscribers who joined during the initial period (later restricted to non-income-tax payers, non-EPFO members).

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Under PMFBY, the sum insured only covers losses from natural calamities before harvesting, not post-harvest losses. 2. PMFBY covers post-harvest losses for crops kept in the field for drying for a specified period. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct — PMFBY covers post-harvest losses for specified crops damaged due to defined perils within a set period after harvesting, in addition to pre-harvest risks.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. PFRDA regulates only the National Pension System and has no role in regulating the Atal Pension Yojana. 2. PFRDA also approves and regulates pension fund managers under NPS. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — PFRDA regulates both NPS and APY. Statement 2 is correct — PFRDA approves and regulates the pension fund managers that invest NPS/APY corpus.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements regarding insurance in India: 1. LIC has a government-guaranteed sovereign backing for its policies under a special Act. 2. Private life insurance companies operating in India do not have any such sovereign guarantee. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct — the LIC Act, 1956 provides a sovereign guarantee on LIC policies, a feature not available to private insurers regulated purely under the Insurance Act/IRDAI framework.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is/are objectives of IRDAI as per the IRDA Act, 1999? 1. Protecting the interests of policyholders. 2. Regulating, promoting and ensuring orderly growth of the insurance industry. 3. Directly setting the fiscal deficit target for the government. How many of the above are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are core objectives of IRDAI. Statement 3 is incorrect — fiscal deficit targets fall under the Ministry of Finance/FRBM framework, not IRDAI's mandate.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Under NPS, both Tier I and Tier II accounts are mandatory for a government subscriber. 2. Withdrawals from Tier II accounts can be made freely, similar to a savings account. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — only Tier I is mandatory; Tier II is voluntary. Statement 2 is correct — Tier II functions like a flexible savings account with no withdrawal restrictions.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Reinsurance means an insurance company transferring part of its risk to another insurer to reduce its own exposure. 2. GIC Re is the only reinsurer permitted to operate in India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 correctly defines reinsurance. Statement 2 is incorrect — foreign reinsurance branches are also permitted to operate in India alongside GIC Re, following liberalisation.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Old Pension Scheme provided pension linked to the last drawn salary of the employee. 2. Under OPS, employees were required to contribute a fixed percentage of salary every month towards their pension fund. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct — OPS pension was linked to the last drawn salary (defined benefit). Statement 2 is incorrect — under OPS, employees did not contribute; the entire pension liability was borne by the government.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about crop insurance premium rates under PMFBY is correct?
o: Premium rates are uniform for all crop categories at 2%
Premium rates vary by crop season/type: 2% for Kharif, 1.5% for Rabi, and 5% for annual commercial/horticultural crops
Premium rates are decided freely by each state without any central norm
There is no premium payable by farmers under PMFBY
intermediate.e: PMFBY prescribes different farmer premium rates by crop category: 2% (Kharif), 1.5% (Rabi), and 5% (commercial/horticultural crops), with the government subsidising the balance actuarial premium.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Health insurance is classified under general insurance in India. 2. Health insurance can be offered exclusively by dedicated standalone health insurers or by general/life insurers as riders. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct — health insurance falls under the general insurance category, and it is offered by standalone health insurers, general insurers, and as riders by life insurers (subject to IRDAI norms).

advanced.q: Which of the following correctly traces the evolution of the FDI limit in the Indian insurance sector?
o: There has never been any FDI cap in insurance
advanced.e: FDI in insurance was initially capped at 26% under the IRDA Act, 1999, raised to 49% in 2015, and further raised to 74% through the Insurance (Amendment) Act, 2021.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Insurance (Amendment) Act, 2021: 1. It raised the FDI limit in Indian insurance companies from 49% to 74%. 2. It removed all requirements regarding Indian ownership and control for insurers with foreign investment. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — even at 74% FDI, safeguards such as a majority of directors and key management persons being resident Indians, and a specified portion of profits being retained as general reserve, continued to apply.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. NPS contributions by an employer are eligible for tax deduction under Section 80CCD(2) of the Income Tax Act, over and above the limit under Section 80C. 2. Atal Pension Yojana subscribers cannot claim any income tax deduction on their contributions. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct — employer's NPS contribution under Section 80CCD(2) is deductible separately from the Section 80C limit. Statement 2 is incorrect — APY contributions are also eligible for tax deduction under Section 80CCD, similar to NPS.

advanced.q: With reference to the National Pension System, consider the following statements: 1. Armed forces personnel are covered under NPS in the same manner as other central government employees. 2. Corporate/private sector employees can voluntarily opt for NPS with employer co-contribution facilitated through the corporate model. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — armed forces personnel are excluded from the mandatory NPS coverage for central government employees. Statement 2 is correct — a corporate model of NPS exists for private/corporate employees.

advanced.q: Which of the following is/are true regarding the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) introduced as an option for central government employees? 1. It guarantees an assured pension linked to average basic pay drawn in the last months of service, subject to minimum qualifying service. 2. It is offered as an alternative to NPS specifically for existing and new central government employees who opt for it, not a replacement of NPS for all. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements broadly describe UPS as approved by the government — it assures a defined pension based on average last-drawn pay (with minimum service conditions) and is offered as an optional alternative to NPS, not a blanket replacement.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements about the difference between disinvestment-era pension reforms and the earlier civil services pension system: 1. Before 2004, the pension liability for government employees was unfunded and met from current revenues (pay-as-you-go). 2. NPS was introduced partly to reduce the growing unfunded pension liability of the government. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct. The pay-as-you-go OPS created a rising unfunded liability, which was a key reason for shifting to the funded, defined-contribution NPS from 2004.

advanced.q: With respect to reinsurance regulation in India, consider the following statements: 1. Foreign reinsurance branches (FRBs) are permitted to set up branch operations in India subject to IRDAI regulations. 2. Indian insurers are required to offer a right of first refusal to GIC Re on reinsurance business up to a specified percentage before approaching other reinsurers. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — FRBs can operate in India under IRDAI norms, and Indian insurers must offer a right of first refusal to the national reinsurer, GIC Re, on a prescribed share of reinsurance business.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. PMFBY is a voluntary scheme for all farmers, including loanee and non-loanee farmers, following reforms made after 2020. 2. Prior to these reforms, PMFBY enrolment was compulsory for farmers who had taken crop loans (loanee farmers). Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct. Originally, PMFBY was compulsory for loanee farmers; reforms made it voluntary for all farmers, including loanee farmers, to increase farmer choice.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. IRDAI's mandate includes specifying obligations of insurers towards rural and social sectors and to certain sections of the population. 2. IRDAI has no role in specifying solvency margin requirements for insurance companies. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct — IRDAI mandates minimum rural/social sector obligations for insurers. Statement 2 is incorrect — IRDAI does prescribe solvency margin requirements to ensure insurers can meet their claim obligations.

advanced.q: With reference to the taxation and withdrawal norms of NPS, consider the following statements: 1. On maturity/exit at superannuation, a subscriber must use at least 40% of the accumulated corpus to purchase an annuity. 2. Up to 60% of the corpus can be withdrawn as a lump sum, which is fully tax-exempt. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct as per current NPS exit norms — a minimum of 40% must go into an annuity, while the remaining 60% lump sum withdrawal is tax-exempt, making NPS an EEE-like instrument at exit for this portion.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains why the Tariff Advisory Committee (TAC) lost significance in India's general insurance market?
o: It was merged with PFRDA to regulate pensions
Detariffication removed mandatory tariff-based pricing, allowing insurers to price most general insurance products based on risk assessment
It was replaced by the Insurance Ombudsman
The government banned all general insurance pricing freedom
advanced.e: With detariffication (progressively from the mid-2000s), insurers gained freedom to price most general insurance products (e.g., motor own-damage, fire, engineering) based on their own risk assessment, reducing the TAC's earlier role in fixing tariffs.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Micro-insurance regulations by IRDAI aim to make low-premium insurance products accessible to low-income groups. 2. Micro-insurance products can be distributed through channels such as NGOs, Self-Help Groups and microfinance institutions. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — IRDAI's micro-insurance framework promotes affordable insurance for low-income households, distributed via NGOs, SHGs, and MFIs acting as intermediaries.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Under PMFBY, the sum insured for a crop is uniform across all districts of a state regardless of production levels. 2. Technology such as remote sensing and smartphone-based crop cutting experiments has been promoted for yield estimation under PMFBY. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — sum insured is linked to the cost of cultivation/scale of finance and can vary by crop and area. Statement 2 is correct — PMFBY has promoted remote sensing and technology-based yield estimation to improve claim settlement accuracy.

advanced.q: Which of the following is the most accurate description of how Atal Pension Yojana determines a subscriber's pension amount?
o: A flat pension amount is given to everyone irrespective of contribution or entry age
The pension amount depends on the subscriber's chosen pension slab, entry age and contribution period
Pension amount is decided solely based on the subscriber's total years of employment
Pension amount is linked to stock market performance each year
advanced.e: Under APY, the monthly contribution required (and hence the guaranteed pension of Rs 1,000–5,000) depends on the subscriber's entry age and chosen pension slab, since younger entrants contribute smaller amounts over a longer period.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. NPS Tier I withdrawal before the age of 60 is entirely prohibited under all circumstances. 2. Partial withdrawal from NPS Tier I is permitted for specified purposes like higher education, marriage of children, or medical treatment, subject to conditions. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — partial withdrawal is permitted under specified conditions, as stated in Statement 2, which is correct, subject to limits (e.g., up to 25% of own contributions) and a minimum period of subscription.

advanced.q: With respect to insurance sector reforms, which of the following sequences is chronologically correct?
o: IRDA Act (1999) -> LIC nationalisation (1956) -> GIC nationalisation (1972)
LIC nationalisation (1956) -> GIC nationalisation (1972) -> IRDA Act (1999)
GIC nationalisation (1972) -> LIC nationalisation (1956) -> IRDA Act (1999)
IRDA Act (1999) -> GIC nationalisation (1972) -> LIC nationalisation (1956)
advanced.e: The correct chronological order is: LIC nationalisation (1956) -> GIC nationalisation (1972) -> IRDA Act, 1999 (which reopened the sector to private participation).

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority approves multiple pension fund managers under NPS, giving subscribers a choice. 2. Under NPS, a subscriber can also choose the asset allocation pattern among equity, corporate debt and government securities, subject to prescribed caps. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — subscribers can choose among PFRDA-approved pension fund managers and can allocate their contribution across equity (E), corporate bonds (C), and government securities (G), subject to prescribed ceilings (e.g., on equity exposure).

advanced.q: Which of the following states have, at various points, announced a return to some form of the Old Pension Scheme for their state government employees, reversing the NPS for state cadres?
o: No state has ever reverted to OPS since NPS is mandated uniformly by the Union Government
Some states such as Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Punjab and Himachal Pradesh announced reversion to OPS for state employees
Only Union Territories can revert to OPS, not states
States can never deviate from NPS as pension is on the Union List
advanced.e: Pension for state government employees is a state subject decision; several states including Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Punjab and Himachal Pradesh at various times announced reversion to OPS for their employees, illustrating that NPS adoption by states is not immutable.

title: Capital Market Instruments
desc: Equity, bonds, derivatives, mutual funds, REITs, InvITs, SGBs

basic.q: What does an equity share primarily represent for its holder?
o: A loan given to the company
A right to buy the company's products at a discount
basic.e: An equity share represents part ownership in a company, entitling the holder to dividends (if declared) and voting rights, but not a fixed guaranteed return.

basic.q: Which of the following best describes a debenture?
o: A share representing ownership in a company
A debt instrument issued by a company acknowledging a loan, generally paying fixed interest
basic.e: A debenture is a debt instrument through which a company borrows money from the public, generally promising fixed periodic interest and repayment of principal.

basic.q: A bond that is not backed by any specific collateral or asset is known as?
basic.e: A bond/debenture without any specific asset backing is called an unsecured bond, relying on the general creditworthiness of the issuer.

basic.q: A financial derivative contract that gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an underlying asset at a predetermined price is called?
basic.e: An option contract gives the buyer a right (not an obligation) to buy (call option) or sell (put option) an asset at a predetermined strike price.

basic.q: A futures contract differs from an options contract mainly in that:
o: Futures give only a right, not an obligation, to trade the underlying asset
Futures create a binding obligation on both parties to transact at a future date at a pre-agreed price
Futures cannot be traded on an exchange
Futures apply only to equity shares, not commodities
basic.e: A futures contract is a binding agreement obligating both the buyer and seller to transact the underlying asset at a specified future date and price, unlike options.

basic.q: A mutual fund pools money from investors and invests it in a diversified portfolio of securities, and is managed by a?
basic.e: A mutual fund scheme is professionally managed by an Asset Management Company (AMC) on behalf of unit holders, under the oversight of a trustee and SEBI regulations.

basic.q: Who regulates mutual funds in India?
basic.e: Mutual funds in India are regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations.

basic.q: REIT stands for?
basic.e: REIT (Real Estate Investment Trust) is an investment vehicle that pools money to invest in income-generating real estate assets and distributes most of the income to investors.

basic.q: InvIT stands for?
basic.e: An Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT) is a vehicle that pools money to invest in completed and revenue-generating infrastructure assets like roads and power transmission lines.

basic.q: Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) are issued by which entity on behalf of the Government of India?
basic.e: Sovereign Gold Bonds are issued by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of the Government of India as government securities denominated in grams of gold.

basic.q: What is the primary purpose of Sovereign Gold Bonds as an investment instrument?
o: To offer an alternative to physically holding gold, while also paying periodic interest
To directly regulate the price of gold in domestic markets
To replace gold jewellery in Indian households
To function purely as a derivative contract on gold futures
basic.e: SGBs allow investors to gain from gold price movements without holding physical gold, while also earning a fixed periodic interest on the initial investment.

basic.q: Which of the following is a key difference between equity and debt instruments?
o: Equity holders are creditors while debt holders are owners
Equity holders are owners bearing residual risk/reward, while debt holders are creditors with a fixed claim
Debt instruments never have a maturity date
Equity guarantees a fixed dividend every year
basic.e: Equity holders are owners who bear residual business risk and potential upside, while debt holders are creditors entitled to fixed interest and repayment, ranking ahead of equity in claims.

basic.q: A 'zero-coupon bond' is a bond that:
o: Pays a very high rate of periodic interest
Pays no periodic interest and is issued at a discount to face value, redeemed at par
Can only be issued by the government
Is another name for an equity share
basic.e: A zero-coupon bond does not pay periodic interest; instead it is issued at a discount and redeemed at face value, with the difference representing the investor's return.

basic.q: A convertible debenture is one which:
o: Can be converted into equity shares of the company after a specified period, as per the terms of issue
Must always be repaid in foreign currency
Cannot ever be transferred to another investor
Pays interest linked to the company's dividend
basic.e: A convertible debenture gives the holder an option (or an obligation, if fully convertible) to convert the debt instrument into equity shares of the issuing company after a specified period.

basic.q: In the mutual fund structure in India, who holds the fiduciary responsibility of ensuring that the assets of the mutual fund are managed in accordance with SEBI regulations and the trust deed?
basic.e: The Trustee holds the mutual fund's assets in trust for the benefit of unit holders and is responsible for ensuring the AMC complies with regulations.

basic.q: What is the minimum lock-in style tenor typically associated with Sovereign Gold Bonds before premature redemption is allowed?
o: The bond has no maturity and no exit option at all
Premature redemption is permitted after the fifth year from the date of issue, on interest payment dates
Premature redemption is allowed only after 20 years
SGBs can be redeemed the next day after purchase
basic.e: SGBs have a tenor of 8 years, with an option for premature redemption from the fifth year onward, exercisable on interest payment dates.

basic.q: Which regulator is responsible for regulating REITs and InvITs listed on Indian stock exchanges?
basic.e: SEBI regulates REITs and InvITs in India through dedicated regulations governing their structure, listing, and disclosure requirements.

basic.q: A 'bond' in the capital market is best described as:
o: A certificate of ownership in a company
A debt security representing a loan made by an investor to a borrower (government or corporate)
A type of savings bank account
A contract to buy an asset at a future date
basic.e: A bond is a debt security through which the issuer (government or corporate) borrows funds from investors and promises repayment with interest.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) in India is correct?
o: REITs are required to distribute a very low proportion of their distributable cash flows to investors
REITs are mandated to distribute at least 90% of their net distributable cash flows to unit holders
REITs cannot be listed on stock exchanges
REITs invest only in raw, non-income generating land
intermediate.e: SEBI regulations require REITs to distribute at least 90% of net distributable cash flows to unit holders, ensuring regular income distribution, and REITs primarily invest in completed, income-generating real estate.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) is correct?
o: InvITs can only invest in under-construction infrastructure projects
InvITs pool investor money to invest in operational, revenue-generating infrastructure assets and distribute income
InvITs are a type of insurance product
intermediate.e: InvITs primarily hold completed and revenue-generating infrastructure assets (e.g., toll roads, power transmission lines), distributing a majority of cash flows to investors, and are regulated by SEBI.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is NOT typically a feature distinguishing derivatives from underlying cash market securities?
o: Derivatives derive their value from an underlying asset
Derivatives can be used for hedging, speculation and arbitrage
Derivatives always require full upfront payment of the entire contract value like cash equity
Futures and options are examples of derivatives
intermediate.e: Unlike cash market equity purchases requiring full payment, derivatives like futures typically require only a margin payment, not the full contract value upfront.

intermediate.q: With regard to mutual fund schemes, an 'open-ended scheme' differs from a 'closed-ended scheme' in that:
o: Open-ended schemes have a fixed maturity date while closed-ended schemes do not
Open-ended schemes allow continuous purchase and redemption of units at NAV-based prices, while closed-ended schemes have a fixed maturity and are typically listed for trading
Closed-ended schemes are always debt schemes only
Open-ended schemes cannot be redeemed at all
intermediate.e: Open-ended schemes allow investors to buy/sell units anytime at NAV-linked prices, while closed-ended schemes have a fixed tenure, with units usually listed on an exchange for secondary market trading.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about Sovereign Gold Bonds is correct?
o: SGBs carry risk of price fluctuation in the value of gold but eliminate the risk and cost of physical gold storage
SGBs are risk-free and their price never fluctuates
SGBs can only be purchased in physical form at jewellery shops
SGBs are a form of equity investment in gold mining companies
intermediate.e: SGBs carry market risk linked to gold prices but remove the risk/cost of storing physical gold, and also provide a fixed periodic interest, which physical gold does not.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about equity vs preference shares is correct?
o: Preference shareholders get dividend priority over equity shareholders but usually do not carry voting rights in normal circumstances
Equity shareholders always get dividends before preference shareholders
Preference shares can never carry a fixed dividend rate
Preference shares are a form of debt instrument, not a share
intermediate.e: Preference shares get priority in dividend payment and capital repayment over equity shares, but generally do not carry voting rights except in specific circumstances (e.g., when dividends are in arrears).

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. In a futures contract, both the buyer and seller are obligated to complete the transaction on the settlement date. 2. In an options contract, only the option writer (seller) has an obligation if the buyer chooses to exercise the option. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct — futures bind both parties, while in options, the buyer has a right (may choose not to exercise) but the seller/writer must honour the contract if exercised.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. A REIT must be listed on a recognised stock exchange in India as per SEBI regulations. 2. A REIT can invest only in commercial real estate and is prohibited from investing in any residential property. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct — SEBI regulations require REIT units to be mandatorily listed. Statement 2 is incorrect — while most Indian REITs so far hold commercial office assets, the regulations do not categorically restrict REITs to commercial real estate alone.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Mutual fund Net Asset Value (NAV) represents the per-unit market value of all the scheme's holdings after deducting liabilities. 2. NAV of a mutual fund scheme remains fixed and does not change on a daily basis. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 correctly defines NAV. Statement 2 is incorrect — NAV is calculated and published typically on each business day, reflecting changes in the value of the underlying portfolio.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Debentures always rank below equity shareholders in case of liquidation of a company. 2. Secured debenture holders have a specific charge on company assets, giving them priority in claims over unsecured creditors. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — debenture holders (creditors) rank above equity shareholders in liquidation. Statement 2 is correct — secured debenture holders have a specific charge providing priority over unsecured creditors.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Sovereign Gold Bonds are issued in demat as well as physical certificate form. 2. Capital gains tax exemption on redemption is available if SGBs are held until final maturity by an individual investor. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct — SGBs can be held in demat or physical (Holding Certificate) form, and capital gains on redemption at final maturity are exempt from tax for individual investors.

intermediate.q: How many of the following are examples of money market instruments (short-term debt instruments), as distinct from capital market instruments? 1. Treasury Bills 2. Commercial Paper 3. Equity shares 4. Certificates of Deposit
intermediate.e: Treasury Bills, Commercial Paper, and Certificates of Deposit are short-term money market instruments; equity shares are a long-term capital market instrument, so three out of four qualify.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. A mutual fund's Exchange Traded Fund (ETF) units are bought and sold on stock exchanges like shares, unlike regular open-ended mutual fund units bought/sold directly with the AMC. 2. ETFs typically track an index and aim to replicate its performance. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct — ETFs trade intraday on exchanges like shares and typically follow a passive strategy tracking an underlying index.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes 'hedging' from 'speculation' in the derivatives market?
o: Hedging seeks to reduce/offset existing price risk, while speculation involves taking on risk in anticipation of profit from price movements
Hedging and speculation are identical strategies with no difference
Speculation is illegal in Indian derivative markets
Hedging always requires holding no underlying asset at all
intermediate.e: Hedging is used to protect against adverse price movements in an existing or anticipated position, whereas speculation involves taking a market view to profit from expected price changes, accepting additional risk.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. InvITs typically raise funds partly from strategic/institutional investors and partly through public offers to retail investors. 2. Cash flows distributed by InvITs to unit holders can include interest, dividend and repayment of debt/capital. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct — InvITs can be privately placed or publicly listed, and their distributions to investors typically comprise a mix of interest, dividend income, and capital repayment.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is/are correct about the role of a 'depository' in the Indian securities market? 1. Depositories hold securities in electronic (dematerialised) form on behalf of investors. 2. NSDL and CDSL are the two depositories operating in India. How many of the above are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct — NSDL and CDSL are India's two depositories that hold securities electronically, eliminating risks associated with physical share certificates.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. A 'rights issue' allows existing shareholders to buy additional shares of the company, usually at a discounted price, in proportion to their current holding. 2. A 'bonus issue' involves the company issuing free additional shares to existing shareholders out of its reserves, without any fresh capital infusion. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements correctly describe rights issues (existing shareholders subscribe to new shares, usually at a discount) and bonus issues (free shares issued by capitalising reserves).

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about 'commercial paper' as a financing instrument is correct?
o: It is a long-term equity instrument used only by government entities
It is a short-term, unsecured money market instrument issued by corporates and highly-rated entities to meet working capital needs
It always carries a maturity of more than 10 years
It can only be issued by public sector banks
intermediate.e: Commercial paper is a short-term (typically up to one year), unsecured promissory note issued by corporates and other eligible entities to raise working-capital funds at competitive rates.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements regarding SEBI's regulatory framework for REITs and InvITs: 1. Both REITs and InvITs are required to hold at least a specified minimum percentage of their assets in completed, revenue-generating assets. 2. Both are structured as trusts with a sponsor, trustee, investment manager, and project manager as key parties. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — SEBI regulations mandate a minimum share of completed revenue-generating assets for REITs/InvITs, and both follow a similar trust structure involving a sponsor, trustee, investment manager, and (for InvITs) project manager.

advanced.q: With reference to Sovereign Gold Bonds, consider the following statements: 1. The redemption price of SGBs is linked to the prevailing market price of gold based on a simple average of closing prices published by a specified body. 2. Interest earned on SGBs is entirely tax-free in the hands of the investor. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct — redemption value is based on the average of closing gold prices (published by an agency such as IBJA) for a specified period. Statement 2 is incorrect — the periodic interest on SGBs is taxable as per the investor's income slab, though the capital gain at maturity is exempt.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. A 'stock split' increases the number of outstanding shares without changing the total market capitalisation of the company, by reducing the face value per share. 2. A 'buyback' of shares by a company reduces the number of outstanding shares and can be carried out through the open market or a tender offer. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — a stock split divides existing shares into smaller denominations without altering overall market value, while a buyback reduces outstanding share count, often to improve return ratios or return surplus cash to shareholders.

advanced.q: With respect to derivative markets in India, consider the following statements: 1. Commodity derivatives were, for a period, regulated by a separate body (Forward Markets Commission) before its merger with SEBI. 2. Currency derivatives on Indian exchanges are permitted for select currency pairs involving the Indian Rupee. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — the Forward Markets Commission (FMC), which regulated commodity derivatives, was merged into SEBI in 2015, and currency derivatives are permitted on exchanges for specified currency pairs against the rupee.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains why InvITs and REITs are often described as instruments that help 'unlock capital' for infrastructure/real estate developers?
o: They give free equity capital to developers with no obligations
They allow developers to monetise completed assets by transferring them to the trust and raising funds from investors, using proceeds to fund new projects or repay debt
They eliminate the need for any regulatory approval to raise funds
They function only as tax-saving instruments with no capital-raising role
advanced.e: By transferring operational assets into a REIT/InvIT structure and selling units to investors, developers can monetise (unlock) locked-in capital from completed projects, redeploying proceeds for new investment or debt reduction — a core rationale behind the National Monetisation Pipeline's use of InvITs.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. In India, both listed InvITs and unlisted (privately placed) InvITs are permitted under SEBI regulations. 2. Public sector entities have used the InvIT structure to monetise operational assets such as national highways and power transmission lines. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — SEBI permits both listed (public) and privately placed InvITs, and public entities like NHAI and PGCIL have used InvITs to monetise highway and transmission assets.

advanced.q: With reference to mutual fund taxation and categorisation, consider the following statements: 1. Equity-oriented mutual fund schemes are those investing a specified minimum proportion of their corpus in domestic equity shares to qualify for equity taxation treatment. 2. Debt mutual funds' taxation treatment has historically differed from equity mutual funds, particularly regarding indexation benefits on long-term gains. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are broadly correct — equity-oriented funds are defined by a minimum domestic equity allocation threshold for tax purposes, and debt fund taxation (including indexation benefits) has historically been treated differently from equity fund taxation, with rules revised over time.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. A 'call option' gives its buyer the right to sell the underlying asset at the strike price. 2. A 'put option' gives its buyer the right to sell the underlying asset at the strike price. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — a call option gives the right to BUY the underlying asset. Statement 2 is correct — a put option gives the right to SELL the underlying asset at the strike price.

advanced.q: Which of the following statements about the difference between 'primary market' and 'secondary market' is most accurate?
o: The primary market deals in trading of already-issued securities among investors, while the secondary market is where new securities are issued
The primary market is where new securities are issued by companies/governments to raise fresh capital, while the secondary market is where existing securities are traded among investors
There is no practical difference between the two markets
Only government securities are traded in the primary market
advanced.e: In the primary market, issuers raise fresh capital by issuing new securities (e.g., IPOs, bond issuances); in the secondary market (e.g., stock exchanges), investors trade already-issued securities among themselves.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Masala Bonds are rupee-denominated bonds issued by Indian entities to overseas investors, where the currency risk is borne by the investor, not the issuer. 2. Masala Bonds are always issued exclusively within the domestic Indian market to resident investors. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct — Masala Bonds are rupee-denominated but issued outside India to foreign investors, who bear the currency risk since repayment is in rupee terms. Statement 2 is incorrect, as they are issued in overseas markets.

advanced.q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs)' Category I, II, and III as per SEBI regulations?
o: Category I invests in start-ups/SMEs/infrastructure with perceived economic benefits; Category II includes funds like private equity/debt funds not falling in I or III; Category III includes funds using complex/diverse trading strategies including derivatives
All three categories are identical in investment strategy
Category III AIFs cannot use leverage or derivatives at all
Category I AIFs are for hedge funds using complex arbitrage strategies
advanced.e: SEBI's AIF Regulations classify Category I (venture capital, SME, infrastructure, social venture funds), Category II (private equity/debt funds without leverage except for operations), and Category III (funds like hedge funds employing diverse/complex strategies, potentially using leverage).

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Government securities (G-Secs) are considered to carry negligible default (credit) risk as they are backed by the sovereign. 2. G-Secs are completely free from price risk if held to maturity by the investor who purchased at issuance. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct — G-Secs carry negligible credit risk due to sovereign backing. Statement 2 is incorrect in a general sense for tradable interest-bearing instruments where market price fluctuates with interest rates, though a buy-and-hold investor does receive the promised coupon/principal; the statement as an absolute claim about 'no price risk' during the holding period from a portfolio valuation perspective is not fully accurate since interim mark-to-market value does fluctuate.

advanced.q: With respect to Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) and index funds, consider the following statements: 1. Both typically follow a passive investment strategy tracking a benchmark index. 2. Unlike index funds, ETF units can be bought or sold throughout the trading day at real-time prices on a stock exchange. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — ETFs and index funds both aim to passively replicate an index, but ETFs, being exchange-listed, allow intraday trading at live market prices, unlike regular index funds transacted at end-of-day NAV.

advanced.q: Which of the following is the most accurate reason why InvITs are considered attractive to long-term investors such as pension and insurance funds?
o: InvITs offer extremely high-risk, high-growth exposure similar to venture capital
InvITs typically hold stable, cash-flow generating infrastructure assets offering relatively predictable and regular distributions, matching long-duration liabilities of such investors
InvITs are guaranteed by the RBI against any loss
InvITs invest exclusively in unlisted start-up equity
advanced.e: Because InvITs hold operational infrastructure assets with predictable cash flows, they suit long-term institutional investors like pension/insurance funds seeking stable income to match their long-duration liabilities.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Perpetual bonds have no fixed maturity date and pay interest indefinitely unless called back by the issuer. 2. Banks in India have used Additional Tier-1 (AT1) perpetual bonds to raise regulatory capital. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — perpetual bonds lack a fixed maturity, and Indian banks have issued AT1 perpetual bonds to shore up regulatory Tier-1 capital, though these carry loss-absorption features making them relatively risky.

advanced.q: Which of the following statements about 'credit rating' of debt instruments is correct?
o: Credit ratings guarantee that the investor will never suffer a loss
Credit ratings are an independent assessment of the issuer's ability and willingness to service debt obligations, but do not eliminate default risk or guarantee repayment
Only the government can assign credit ratings to bonds
Credit ratings apply only to equity shares, not to debt instruments
advanced.e: Credit ratings issued by agencies (e.g., CRISIL, ICRA, CARE) assess relative credit risk/repayment capacity of an issuer but are opinions, not guarantees, and do not eliminate the possibility of default.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. A depository participant (DP) acts as an intermediary between the investor and the depository for holding securities in demat form. 2. An investor must necessarily open a demat account with both NSDL and CDSL to trade in the Indian securities market. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 correctly describes the role of a Depository Participant. Statement 2 is incorrect — an investor needs a demat account with only one depository (either NSDL or CDSL) through a DP, not both.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Real Estate Mutual Funds (REMFs) and REITs are identical instruments with no structural difference. 2. Unlike a REIT, a conventional real estate mutual fund does not necessarily hold direct income-generating property but may invest in real estate securities/companies. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — REITs and real estate mutual funds have distinct regulatory structures. Statement 2 is correct — a conventional real estate-focused mutual fund may invest in shares of real estate/housing finance companies rather than owning physical property directly, unlike a REIT which directly holds real estate assets.

basic.q: What does 'disinvestment' mean in the context of government policy?
o: The government increasing its shareholding in a public sector enterprise
The sale or dilution of government equity/shareholding in a public sector enterprise
Closure of a private company by the government
Government borrowing from public sector banks
basic.e: Disinvestment refers to the sale or dilution of the government's equity stake in a Public Sector Undertaking (PSU), which may or may not result in loss of government control.

basic.q: What is the key difference between 'disinvestment' and 'privatisation'?
o: They mean exactly the same thing in all cases

Privatisation specifically refers to disinvestment that results in transfer of ownership and management control to a private entity, whereas disinvestment can occur even with government retaining majority control
Disinvestment always means 100% sale of a PSU
basic.e: Privatisation is a form of disinvestment where control/management passes to a private entity (e.g., through sale of 51% or more, or via strategic sale), whereas disinvestment more broadly includes partial stake sales where government retains control.

basic.q: Which government department is primarily responsible for managing disinvestment of central PSUs in India?
o: Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM)
basic.e: The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM), under the Ministry of Finance, manages central government disinvestment and PSU asset monetisation.

basic.q: DIPAM was earlier known by which name before being renamed?
basic.e: DIPAM was earlier called the Department of Disinvestment and was renamed and given an expanded mandate in 2016.

basic.q: Which classification category represents the highest tier of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) in India, granting the greatest financial and operational autonomy?
basic.e: Maharatna is the highest category of CPSEs, granting them enhanced financial autonomy, including higher investment limits without seeking government approval.

basic.q: The 'Navratna' status for CPSEs was introduced in which decade?
basic.e: The Navratna scheme was introduced in 1997 (1990s) to grant greater autonomy to select high-performing CPSEs.

basic.q: Which body grants Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna status to CPSEs?
o: Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), Ministry of Finance
basic.e: The Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) under the Ministry of Finance/Ministry of Heavy Industries lays down criteria and grants Maharatna/Navratna/Miniratna status.

basic.q: Which of the following is an example of 'strategic disinvestment' undertaken by the Government of India, involving transfer of management control?
o: Sale of a small minority stake in a PSU through an offer for sale on the stock exchange
Air India's sale to the Tata Group
Payment of dividend by a PSU to the government
Government buying back its own shares in a PSU
basic.e: The sale of Air India to the Tata Group, involving 100% stake sale along with management control, is a classic example of strategic disinvestment.

basic.q: What is the National Monetisation Pipeline (NMP)?
o: A plan for privatising all public sector banks
A pipeline for physically transporting monetary currency across India
A framework for monetising the government's core operating brownfield infrastructure assets by unlocking value while retaining ownership
A scheme for direct tax collection
basic.e: The National Monetisation Pipeline is a strategy to unlock value from operational (brownfield) public infrastructure assets through instruments like leasing/InvITs, without transferring ownership.

basic.q: Under the National Monetisation Pipeline, is ownership of the underlying asset transferred to the private party?
o: No, the government/public entity retains ownership; only the right to operate and collect revenue for a fixed period is typically transferred
Ownership is transferred to a foreign government
The private party gets a permanent free grant of the asset
basic.e: Under the NMP, the government/public entity retains ownership of the underlying assets, while the private party is typically given the right to operate and monetise the asset for a defined concession period.

basic.q: Which of the following ministries/departments launched the National Monetisation Pipeline in 2021?
o: Ministry of Finance (NITI Aayog in coordination with line ministries)
basic.e: The National Monetisation Pipeline was unveiled in 2021, prepared by NITI Aayog in coordination with various infrastructure line ministries.

basic.q: A CPSE must generally have how many consecutive years of profit, among other criteria, to be considered for Navratna status?
basic.e: Among other financial criteria, a CPSE is generally required to have posted profits in three of the last five years to be eligible for Navratna status (criteria are periodically reviewed by DPE).

basic.q: Which of these is the lowest of the three CPSE autonomy categories (Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna)?
basic.e: Miniratna is the lowest of the three categories, still granting some financial autonomy compared to CPSEs with no special status.

basic.q: 'Minority stake sale' as a mode of disinvestment refers to:
o: Sale of a government stake such that government still retains majority ownership and management control
Complete exit of government from the enterprise
Sale of the enterprise to another PSU only
Free transfer of shares to employees only
basic.e: In a minority stake sale, the government dilutes only a part of its holding while retaining majority ownership (51% or more) and management control.

basic.q: Which of the following was one of India's earliest major economic reforms (1991-92) that paved the way for greater private participation and disinvestment in PSUs?
basic.e: The New Industrial Policy of 1991 reduced the scope of industries reserved exclusively for the public sector and initiated the disinvestment process as part of broader liberalisation.

basic.q: An Initial Public Offer (IPO) or Offer for Sale (OFS) of a PSU's shares to the public, where the government retains majority stake, is an example of which type of disinvestment?
basic.e: When the government sells a portion of its stake via IPO/OFS but retains majority ownership, it constitutes minority stake sale/non-strategic disinvestment, as opposed to a change in management control.

basic.q: Which of the following best defines 'nationalisation'?
o: Transfer of ownership of a private enterprise/industry to government/public ownership
Transfer of a government enterprise to private ownership
Sale of shares only to foreign investors
basic.e: Nationalisation is the opposite of privatisation — it involves the government taking over ownership and control of a privately owned enterprise or industry.

basic.q: Proceeds from disinvestment of CPSEs are credited to which fund for utilisation as per extant government policy?
o: Consolidated Fund of India directly for general expenditure with no separate accounting
National Investment Fund (NIF), later modified for use as per government-approved policy including capital expenditure
basic.e: Disinvestment proceeds were routed through the National Investment Fund (NIF), with its usage policy amended over time to allow greater flexibility, including funding capital expenditure of the government.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about Maharatna CPSEs is correct?
o: Maharatna CPSEs require prior government approval for all capital expenditure regardless of amount
Maharatna CPSEs enjoy enhanced financial autonomy, including higher ceilings on capital expenditure and investment in joint ventures/subsidiaries without government approval
Maharatna status can be granted to private companies as well
Maharatna is a classification used only for banks
intermediate.e: Maharatna CPSEs are granted greater financial autonomy including higher investment ceilings for capital expenditure, joint ventures and subsidiaries, without needing case-by-case government approval, subject to board approval.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about the National Monetisation Pipeline (NMP) is correct?
o: NMP involves outright sale of government assets to private players
NMP involves leasing out revenue rights of operational government assets to private entities for a fixed period, without transferring ownership
NMP applies only to public sector banks
NMP is unrelated to infrastructure assets
intermediate.e: NMP is based on the concept of 'monetisation, not sale' — the government leases out the right to operate/collect revenue from brownfield assets (roads, railways, power, etc.) for a defined period while retaining ownership.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is/are correct distinctions between 'strategic disinvestment' and 'minority stake sale'? 1. Strategic disinvestment involves transfer of management control to a private buyer along with substantial equity. 2. Minority stake sale means selling a stake without giving up government control. How many of the above are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements correctly capture the essential distinction — strategic disinvestment transfers management control (usually with 50%+ equity/majority stake sale to a private/strategic buyer), while a minority stake sale retains government control.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Public sector banks are classified under the Maharatna/Navratna/Miniratna scheme just like manufacturing and services CPSEs. 2. The Maharatna/Navratna/Miniratna classification applies specifically to Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs), not banks or financial institutions. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct — the Maharatna/Navratna/Miniratna scheme, administered by the Department of Public Enterprises, applies to non-financial CPSEs, not to public sector banks, which have their own separate governance framework.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Air India strategic sale in 2021 involved transfer of 100% government equity along with management control to Tata Sons. 2. Under this transaction, all of Air India's legacy debt was fully waived off with no liability transferred to the buyer. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct — 100% government stake in Air India was transferred to Tata Sons along with management control. Statement 2 is incorrect — the transaction involved the buyer taking over a defined portion of Air India's debt, not a complete waiver.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about the objectives of disinvestment is correct?
o: Disinvestment aims solely to shut down loss-making PSUs permanently
Disinvestment aims to mobilise resources for the government, improve efficiency through private participation/market discipline, and reduce the fiscal burden of running non-strategic enterprises
Disinvestment is done only to increase government control over the economy
Disinvestment applies only to state government companies, not central PSUs
intermediate.e: Disinvestment is undertaken with multiple objectives including resource mobilisation, unlocking value, improving efficiency via private participation, and reducing the burden of running enterprises in non-strategic sectors.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Under India's PSU policy framework, sectors are broadly classified into 'strategic' and 'non-strategic', with a stated policy of maintaining bare minimum presence in strategic sectors and privatising/closing units in non-strategic sectors. 2. Atomic energy and space are examples of sectors identified as strategic, where a significant government presence continues. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct — India's public sector enterprise policy (from 2021) categorises sectors into strategic and non-strategic, with sectors such as atomic energy, space and defence identified among the strategic sectors warranting continued public sector presence.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Miniratna Category-I and Category-II CPSEs have different financial autonomy limits, with Category-I generally enjoying higher limits than Category-II. 2. A CPSE can be simultaneously classified as both Navratna and Miniratna. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct — Miniratna Category-I CPSEs are given somewhat higher autonomy limits than Category-II. Statement 2 is incorrect — these are distinct, mutually exclusive classification tiers; a CPSE holds only one status at a time.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is a correct example pairing of a disinvestment/PSU-related term with its meaning?
o: 'Buyback of shares' — government injecting fresh equity capital into a loss-making PSU
'Strategic sale' — sale of substantial government shareholding along with transfer of management control to a private buyer identified through a competitive process
'Golden share' — a share that pays the highest dividend among all PSU shares
'Demerger' — merging of two separate PSUs into one combined entity
intermediate.e: Strategic sale correctly refers to the sale of a substantial government shareholding together with management control, typically identified through a competitive bidding process.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Listing of a CPSE's shares on the stock exchange automatically implies privatisation of that CPSE. 2. Government can list a CPSE's minority stake on an exchange while still retaining majority ownership and control. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — mere listing does not amount to privatisation if government retains majority control. Statement 2 is correct and describes a common form of minority stake sale/listing disinvestment.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the rationale behind granting greater autonomy to Maharatna/Navratna CPSEs?
o: To enable them to compete globally and take timely investment decisions without excessive bureaucratic delay, while remaining accountable to their boards and government oversight
To allow them to completely escape any government oversight or auditing requirements
To convert them immediately into private companies
To reduce their profitability through mandatory price controls
intermediate.e: Enhanced autonomy for Maharatna/Navratna CPSEs is intended to enable faster, competitive decision-making (on capital expenditure, JVs, subsidiaries) while remaining accountable through board processes and government oversight mechanisms like performance agreements.

intermediate.q: How many of the following are typically cited as modes/routes of disinvestment used by the Government of India? 1. Initial Public Offering (IPO) 2. Offer for Sale (OFS) through stock exchange 3. Strategic sale to a private buyer 4. Exchange Traded Fund (ETF) route bundling PSU shares
intermediate.e: All four — IPOs, OFS, strategic sale, and the CPSE/Bharat 22 ETF route — have been used by the Government of India as disinvestment mechanisms over the years.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The National Monetisation Pipeline covers only central government assets and excludes any state government or PSU assets. 2. Asset classes under the NMP include roads, railways, power transmission, telecom, mining, and warehousing infrastructure, among others. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — while primarily focused on central government/CPSE assets, the monetisation approach set an example intended to extend more broadly. Statement 2 is correct, as the NMP spans a diverse set of infrastructure asset classes across sectors like roads, railways, power, telecom and mining.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is the most appropriate description of 'disinvestment target' as used in the Union Budget?
o: A binding legal commitment that the government must always meet exactly
The estimated receipts the government expects to mobilise during a financial year from disinvestment of its stake in CPSEs/other assets, which are budget estimates subject to revision
A fixed number of PSUs that must be sold every year without exception
An indicator only of foreign investment inflow
intermediate.e: The disinvestment target set in the Union Budget is an estimate of expected receipts from stake sales during the fiscal year; actual realisation often varies from the budgeted target depending on market conditions and transaction timelines.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. A CPSE losing its Navratna/Maharatna status can, in principle, be downgraded if it fails to meet the prescribed performance criteria on a sustained basis. 2. The criteria for Maharatna/Navratna/Miniratna status include parameters such as net worth, turnover, and net profit over a period of years. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct — status can be reviewed/withdrawn if performance criteria are not sustained, and the criteria involve financial parameters like net worth, turnover and net profit over a specified period.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about privatisation of public sector banks (PSBs) in India is correct?
o: All PSBs were privatised immediately after bank nationalisation in 1969

The government has, as part of broader disinvestment/reform policy, considered and undertaken consolidation and selective privatisation-related reforms for PSBs, distinct from the CPSE Maharatna framework
PSBs cannot legally be privatised under any circumstances
Privatisation of PSBs is regulated by DIPAM using the same Maharatna criteria as manufacturing CPSEs
intermediate.e: Reform of public sector banks, including consolidation and consideration of selective privatisation, has been pursued as a distinct policy track from the CPSE Maharatna/Navratna framework, which does not apply to banks.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best describes the role of transaction advisors/asset monetisation advisors engaged by the government in disinvestment and monetisation transactions?
o: They have no role and are only symbolic appointees
They assist in valuation, structuring, due diligence and managing the bidding process for disinvestment/monetisation transactions on behalf of the government
They directly decide the final buyer without government approval
They are responsible only for post-sale employee grievance redressal
intermediate.e: Transaction advisors (often investment banks/consultancies) are engaged to assist with valuation, deal structuring, due diligence and managing the competitive bidding process in disinvestment/monetisation deals.

intermediate.q: Which of the following is an example of a PSU where the government undertook disinvestment through listing on the stock exchange while retaining majority ownership, rather than a strategic sale?
o: IPO/listing of PSUs such as coal, power or insurance companies with government retaining majority stake
Sale of Bharat Petroleum's stake with full management control transfer (proposed)
Complete closure of a sick PSU
intermediate.e: Several CPSEs (e.g., in coal, power, insurance sectors) have been listed via IPOs where the government retained majority ownership, representing minority stake sale/non-strategic disinvestment, distinct from a full strategic sale like Air India.

advanced.q: With reference to the evolution of India's disinvestment policy, consider the following statements: 1. In the initial phase of disinvestment (early 1990s), the approach largely involved sale of minority stakes through auctions to financial institutions/public, rather than management control transfer. 2. From the early 2000s, the policy shift towards 'strategic sale' allowed transfer of management control in select PSUs to private strategic partners. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements correctly trace the evolution — early disinvestment (post-1991) largely involved minority stake sales, while from around 1999-2000 onward, the government explicitly adopted a policy permitting strategic sales with transfer of management control in select cases.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 2021 Public Sector Enterprise (PSE) policy: 1. It envisages privatisation or closure of CPSEs in non-strategic sectors, subject to feasibility. 2. It calls for maintaining a 'bare minimum presence' of the public sector even in strategic sectors, implying some CPSEs may still be privatised, merged or brought under holding structures even within strategic sectors. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — the 2021 PSE policy calls for privatisation/closure of CPSEs in non-strategic sectors, while even in strategic sectors, it envisages retaining only a bare minimum presence, implying scope for consolidation or privatisation of some units even there.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Strategic disinvestment necessarily requires the buyer to be a domestic (Indian) private entity only. 2. Strategic disinvestment transactions in India have, in specific cases, allowed foreign entities/promoters to participate as bidders, subject to sectoral FDI norms. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — there is no blanket requirement restricting strategic sale buyers to only Indian entities. Statement 2 is correct — participation is generally permitted subject to applicable sectoral FDI policy and other regulatory approvals.

advanced.q: With reference to the National Monetisation Pipeline (NMP), consider the following statements: 1. The instruments used for monetisation under NMP include structures such as Toll-Operate-Transfer (TOT), Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs), and long-term leasing. 2. Once an asset is monetised under NMP, the government permanently loses the right to reclaim operational control at the end of the concession period. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct — NMP uses instruments like TOT, InvITs, and long-term leasing. Statement 2 is incorrect — since ownership remains with the public entity, control/operational rights revert back to it at the end of the defined concession period.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains why the government retains a Maharatna/Navratna classification framework instead of privatising all profitable CPSEs uniformly?
o: The classification is purely symbolic, with no bearing on actual operational or financial autonomy

It allows the government to grant graded operational and financial autonomy to well-performing CPSEs that continue to operate in sectors where continued public ownership is considered strategically or socially important, while enabling them to compete effectively
It is a legal requirement under the Companies Act, 2013 for all government companies
It replaced the need for any disinvestment policy altogether
advanced.e: The Maharatna/Navratna/Miniratna framework enables the government to grant graded autonomy to CPSEs so they can compete and invest efficiently, while allowing continued public ownership in sectors deemed strategically or socially significant, as opposed to blanket privatisation.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Under the CPSE Exchange Traded Fund (ETF) route, the government bundles shares of multiple CPSEs into a single fund unit that is offered to investors, thereby diluting its stake across several PSUs simultaneously. 2. This route is classified as a form of strategic disinvestment since it results in loss of majority government control over the bundled CPSEs. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 correctly describes the CPSE ETF mechanism. Statement 2 is incorrect — the ETF route typically involves only minority stake dilution across multiple CPSEs, with the government retaining majority control; it is not strategic disinvestment.

advanced.q: With respect to the distinction between 'disinvestment receipts' and 'dividends' received by the government from CPSEs, consider the following statements: 1. Dividends are a recurring return on the government's equity investment paid out of a CPSE's distributable profits. 2. Disinvestment receipts arise from a one-time (or periodic) sale of the government's equity stake and represent capital receipts, not revenue receipts. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct — dividends are recurring revenue receipts from CPSE profits, whereas disinvestment proceeds are treated as capital receipts in government accounts since they arise from the sale of an asset (equity stake).

advanced.q: Which of the following statements accurately distinguishes 'privatisation' from mere 'corporatisation' of a government department/undertaking?
o: Corporatisation converts a government department into a company (often wholly government-owned) to bring in commercial/managerial autonomy, without necessarily transferring ownership to private hands, unlike privatisation which involves transfer of ownership/control to private entities
